title: Literature check: phoretic Janus composites are Soto-Golestanian active colloidal molecules (known); their growth and B-band division on a food ledger has no published match found; Romano et al. 2026 report self-propelling multi-species droplet clusters even with purely attractive nonreciprocity; Marangoni nematic rods are a variant of Giomi-DeSimone
summary: Opened four primary abstracts. Soto & Golestanian 2014 (self-assembled catalytic colloidal molecules that move or spin) is the known mechanism behind c33's SIM composites. Agudo-Canalejo & Golestanian 2019 give the general nonreciprocal multi-species model without growth or division, so c33's food-ledger division is a variant at least and possibly new. Romano et al. 2026 (PRL) show self-propelling clusters of droplets of different species even under purely attractive nonreciprocal interactions, from nonlocality. Giomi & DeSimone 2014 is the base of the nematic rods. One question raised: attractive-only nonreciprocal phoretic cells as a route to a wall.
